title: writing
summary: how people learned to store words outside their heads: from clay tokens to alphabets, paper, printing, and screens.

title: money and trade
summary: debts in silver, the first coins, camel caravans and monsoon ships, paper money, and a world economy tied together by silver, slavery, and steam.

title: energy
summary: every age of history has run on some source of power: muscle, fire, wind and water, coal, oil, the atom, and now the sun again.

title: disease and medicine
summary: plagues have killed more people than wars. this is the story of how they spread, and how people slowly learned to fight back.

title: migration
summary: humans have always been on the move: out of africa, across oceans, along the steppe, in chains, and in search of a better life.

title: belief
summary: from careful burials and painted caves to the great world religions and modern secular states: how people have answered the biggest questions.

title: science
summary: how many peoples, over thousands of years, built up a way of finding out how the world works by watching, measuring, and testing.

title: cities
summary: from the first walled towns to megacities of thirty million: why people crowd together, and what it has cost and given them.
